acceptanceCriteria: Build retains at most a fixed number of frontier entries (with an explicit omission count) so live heap for the 4096x2000 repro stays bounded, proven by a failing-before test.
The CLI build and --check agree on accept/refuse for the repro shape, or the divergence is specified in DCP-V1-044.
body: Found in the #717 adapter-check review (claude/gh717-adapter-check 53b6c3ab, round 6). BuildBehaviorAdapter (internal/doccorpus/behavior_adapter.go, gap/gapFromInput via reconcile) appends one frontier diagnostic per missing outcome per test with no cap. Repro: helper behaviorAdapterOutcomeFrontierRequest(t, N, M) in internal/doccorpus/behavior_adapter_check_test.go (valid fixture, observations cleared, one variation with N outcomes and empty testKeys, M tests whose criterionKeys reference it). Measured: 4096x200 (787,469 B input) -> 820,607 entries, 204 MiB live heap; 4096x400 (1,067,269 B) -> 1,641,207 entries, 404 MiB; linear ~255 B/entry, so 4096x2000 (within request bounds) extrapolates to ~2 GiB (inference, not run). Expected: frontier bounded (count cap with omission marker) so Build memory is bounded by its output bound. Actual: unbounded retention; library Build returns nil but CLI `corvint docs corpus` build then fails Encode with corpus-refused output bound exceeded (cmd/corvint/docs_corpus.go ~228), so --check (which skips reconciliation since 53b6c3ab) accepts what the CLI build refuses.
